title: One shared badge/chip primitive, not a per-feature -badge class
statement: Small status or metadata indicators (badges, chips, pills) reuse one shared badge component or utility class parameterized by variant; a feature does not define its own `.<feature>-badge`/`.<feature>-chip` CSS class that reimplements the same visual pattern.
rationale: This is the operator-observed defect class: no component reuse. The app currently carries at least four independently styled badge-like primitives (`.anchor-badge`, `.scope-exclusion-badge`, `.quota-chip`, `.embedded-badge`) across different feature folders, each redeclaring padding/radius/font-size instead of consuming a shared token-driven primitive. A shared primitive also gets QS-NG-003 token compliance for free instead of four times over.

good.caption: Target shape: one shared badge primitive, varied by input.

bad.caption: Four independently declared badge/chip classes with overlapping geometry. The two shown in full are from the cited app.css; `.anchor-badge` is in frontend/src/app/editor/editor.css and `.scope-exclusion-badge` in frontend/src/app/explorer/explorer.css.

changelog.summary: Initial rule; bad example lists the real duplicated badge/chip classes found across feature stylesheets.
